title: Promotion: a pawn on the last rank
outcomes: Promotes a pawn to a queen when told
Promotes by capturing when the square ahead is blocked
Says when a pawn cannot promote on this move
Notices that a queen is not always the best choice (preview only)

steps.text: You just **promoted**. A pawn that reaches the far edge, the **last rank**, cannot stay a pawn: in the same move it becomes a **queen, rook, bishop or knight** of its own colour, your choice (never a king). The queen is the usual pick because it is the strongest piece. Watch a pawn make the last of the trip.

steps.caption: A lone pawn marches to the last rank and changes into a queen.

line.say: One step puts the pawn next to the last rank.
Black's king is too far from d8 to stop it.
The pawn reaches the last rank and becomes a queen.

claims.statement: After the march a white queen stands on d8.

steps.text: A pawn reaches the last rank by moving **straight ahead** onto an empty square, or by **capturing one step diagonally forward**. It never captures straight ahead. When a piece blocks the square in front, look at the two diagonals: an enemy piece there lets the pawn promote by capturing.

steps.caption: The knight still blocks the way, but now an enemy rook stands diagonally ahead.

line.say: The pawn captures the rook and becomes a queen in the same move.

claims.statement: The capture and promotion is legal.
The straight move is blocked by the knight.

steps.caption: This pawn is still two steps from the last rank. It needs two moves.

line.say: One step: the pawn is now on the rank before the last, but it has not promoted yet.
Only now does the pawn reach the last rank and promote.

claims.statement: The pawn cannot jump two squares from here.

steps.caption: Preview, not a rule to learn yet: the queen is only the usual choice. Here a knight gives checkmate, because it checks the king and covers b6 while Black's own pieces fill the other squares. A queen on c8 is not mate: Black still has moves.

line.say: Checkmate: the knight gives check, and the king has no square and no capture.

steps.text: **Model answer.** A pawn reaching the last rank becomes a queen, rook, bishop or knight in the same move. It gets there by moving straight onto an empty square or by capturing one step diagonally forward. A pawn two or more steps away needs more moves first. The queen is usual; the knight mate was a preview of another choice.

steps.prompt: Read the model answer, cover it, then explain to a friend how a pawn promotes and the two ways it can reach the last rank.
